chapter: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
title: Lorraine Gardens, the Dreamland crowd and bootleg liquor
summary: The Lorraine was lower class; the Dreamland drew downtown people, pimps and gangsters, with concealed bootleg whiskey and raids.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Did you ever go to the Lorraine Gardens?
Oh, yes, I went to the Lorraine Gardens.
Now the Lorraine, from what I understand, was sort of a slightly lower class than Dreamland?
Oh, yes. Oh, yes, it was, sort of lower class during that time. That was when the Dreamland was very popular, it was lower class type of a place.
Now, what kind of people came into

Well the Dreamland was -- it was on State Street, kind of out of the way from the other clubs. And they had quite a lot of kind of people from downtown. Came to the Dreamland. Mostly lot -- in other words, it was like the Congress Inn, here, compared with that. And quite a lot of pimps and gangsters.
And what -- now this is during the Prohibition, of course, and what -- they didn't serve lemonade, did they?
No. Well they just served whiskey, bootleg whiskey. And beer, bootleg beer.
Uh-huh. So that subjected them to raids, I would imagine?
Oh, yes. They were often raided, raided every now and then, yes.
And was the liquor served openly?
No, not openly, no. You know you could get it, the waiter would bring it in like a pint, something like that a quart. I f you pay for it, but they wasn't serving it openly, no. But it --
Concealed, yes. And also you could bring your own bottle in.
Sit it down on the floor.
